items.name: Return flights London ⇄ Bangkok
items.note: Typical economy return fare; usually £450-750, cheapest in Feb-Mar and Oct, most expensive in December.

items.name: Backpacker travel insurance
items.note: Per month. Needs cover for scooters (with a licence), diving and adventure activities, and medical evacuation.

items.name: eSIM data (per country, 30 days)
items.note: e.g. Airalo or Holafly, about 10GB for 30 days. Or buy a local SIM at the airport for less.

items.name: International Driving Permit (1949)
items.note: From the Post Office. Covers Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

items.name: International Driving Permit (1968) - Vietnam
items.note: Vietnam only accepts the 1968 IDP. Only needed if you'll ride in Vietnam.

items.name: Hep A, Typhoid, Tetanus/Diphtheria/Polio
items.note: Free on the NHS - book through your GP practice nurse 6-8 weeks before you go.

items.name: Rabies vaccine (3 doses)
items.note: About £60-75 per dose. Strongly recommended for long trips and scooter riders.

items.name: Japanese encephalitis (2 doses)
items.note: About £100 per dose. Recommended for long stays in rural SEA.

items.name: Hepatitis B (3 doses)
items.note: Optional - recommended for tattoos, medical work or volunteering.

items.name: Malaria tablets
items.note: Usually not needed for the main SEA backpacker routes - ask the travel clinic.

items.name: Packing cubes, padlock, towel, dry bag, headtorch
Toiletries & suncream to start
items.note: Suncream is expensive in SEA - bring some from home.

items.name: Fee-free travel card (Wise/Revolut/Monzo/Starling)
items.note: Avoids 3% foreign fees. Expect local ATM fees of about £5 per withdrawal in Thailand and Cambodia.

items.name: ATM fees on the road
items.note: Thai ATMs charge 220 THB per withdrawal - withdraw larger amounts less often.

items.name: Emergency fund
items.note: For missed flights, a lost phone or medical excess. Keep it untouched if possible.
